title: Kinetic Theory
seo_title: Kinetic Theory Class 11 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 12)

body_html:
How to think about it

An ideal gas obeys pV = nRT (R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹), which includes Boyle's and Charles's laws. Kinetic theory explains pressure as molecules hitting the walls: p = ⅓ρv²rms. The average kinetic energy of a molecule is (3/2)kT, so temperature measures molecular motion.

Each degree of freedom has an average energy of ½kT (equipartition). A monatomic gas has 3 and Cv = 3R/2; a rigid diatomic gas has 5 and Cv = 5R/2. The mean free path is the average distance between collisions.

Example

v(rms) when T becomes 4T?

v ∝ √T

Answer: doubles

Example

Degrees of freedom of O₂?

3 + 2

Answer: 5

Common mistakes

  • Using °C instead of kelvin in pV = nRT.
  • Thinking rms speed is proportional to T.
  • Giving a diatomic gas 3 degrees of freedom.

faq.q: How does kinetic theory explain temperature?
faq.a: The absolute temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the molecules: (3/2)kT.

faq.q: What is the law of equipartition of energy?
faq.a: In equilibrium each degree of freedom of a molecule has an average energy of ½kT.
